newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan expected to pass motor insurance law.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan expected to pass motor insurance law.

text.p: Taiwan's parliament is likely to pass a bill requiring third-party liability insurance for motorists thanks to the mother of a road accident victim, the United Daily News said on Thursday.

Stalled in parliament for more than four years, the bill got new life on Wednesday when President Lee Teng-hui met a woman who has waged a campaign for mandatory insurance since her son was killed by an uninsured truck driver in 1989.
"I was moved by your selfless, merciful heart," Lee was quoted as telling parent-turned-lobbyist Ko-Tsai Yu-chiung.
For the past 33 weeks, Ko has protested outside the building where the ruling Nationalist Party holds its weekly meeting.

After meeting Ko, Lee urged ruling party deputies to step up efforts to enact the bill. Two major opposition parties also pledged support, setting the stage for a final parliamentary reading next week at the earliest, the newspaper said.

Ko has pressed the government to enact a law mandating that all vehicle drivers buy third-party liability insurance under which compensation would be paid to victims regardless of whether the motorist or the injured person was responsible.
The cabinet drafted the current bill in 1992.
